pairs.question: I feel like quitting smoking is really hard. Is there any support available?
pairs.answer: Yes, smokers usually have a much better chance of quitting with a support program. These programs are offered by hospitals, health departments, community centers, work sites, and national organizations.
pairs.evidence: Smokers usually have a much better chance of quitting with a support program. Stop smoking programs are offered by hospitals, health departments, community centers, work sites, and national organizations.

pairs.question: What makes a smoking cessation program effective?
pairs.answer: The most effective smoking cessation programs combine more than one approach and target the fears and problems you have when quitting. They also provide ongoing support for staying away from tobacco.
pairs.evidence: The most effective smoking cessation programs combine more than one approach and target the fears and problems you have when quitting. They also provide ongoing support for staying away from tobacco.

pairs.question: Are there specific times when I can call for help with quitting?
pairs.answer: Yes, telephone programs are often available on nights and weekends. You can reach out for support when it’s convenient for you.
pairs.evidence: Telephone programs are often available on nights and weekends.

pairs.question: Can I get support from my doctor while trying to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, you can seek support from your primary care provider or nurse. They can provide guidance and help you through the quitting process.
pairs.evidence: You may also want to seek out other types of support, such as: Your primary care provider or nurse.

pairs.question: What is a support group for quitting smoking like?
pairs.answer: A support group for quitting smoking uses a similar approach as Alcoholics Anonymous. You’ll be asked to admit that you are powerless over your addiction to nicotine.
pairs.evidence: This organization uses a similar approach as Alcoholics Anonymous. As part of this group, you will be asked to admit that you are powerless over your addiction to nicotine.

pairs.question: What tools do stop smoking programs offer to help me cope?
pairs.answer: These programs offer tools to cope with the problems that arise while trying to quit. They can help you avoid making common mistakes.
pairs.evidence: They will help you be aware of problems that come up while you're trying to quit and offer tools to cope with these problems.

pairs.question: How long should each session in a smoking cessation program last?
pairs.answer: Each session should last at least 15 to 30 minutes. This is important for effective support during your quit journey.
pairs.evidence: Each session lasts at least 15 to 30 minutes.

pairs.question: What is the minimum duration for a smoking cessation program?
pairs.answer: The program should last at least 2 weeks, but longer is usually better. This gives you more time to build your quitting skills.
pairs.evidence: The program lasts at least 2 weeks, although longer is usually better.

pairs.question: What kind of training should the leader of a smoking cessation program have?
pairs.answer: The leader should be trained in smoking cessation. This ensures you receive the best guidance possible.
pairs.evidence: The leader is trained in smoking cessation.

pairs.question: Are there online options for quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, internet-based programs are becoming more available. They can send you personalized reminders through email or texting.
pairs.evidence: Internet-based programs are also becoming more available. These services send you personalized reminders using e-mail, texting, or other methods.

pairs.question: What types of counseling formats are available in smoking cessation programs?
pairs.answer: Programs may have one-on-one sessions or group counseling, and some offer both. You can choose what feels right for you.
pairs.evidence: Programs may either have one-on-one sessions or group counseling. Some programs offer both.

pairs.question: What is a feature of successful smoking cessation programs?
pairs.answer: Programs that provide more sessions or longer sessions have a better chance of success. More support can really make a difference.
pairs.evidence: Programs that provide more sessions or longer sessions have a better chance of success.

pairs.question: Where can I find more information about quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: You can visit the American Cancer Society website for more resources. They have a lot of helpful information on quitting.
pairs.evidence: American Cancer Society website. Stay away from tobacco.
